summary: This Wikipedia-derived note lists characters from the sitcom That '70s Show, focusing on Pam Macy and Steven Hyde. It covers Pam's episode appearances and the Kelso prom and 'Romantic Weekend' storylines, the ending where Eric and Donna reunite, and Hyde's personality, relationships with Jackie and Samantha, and discovery of his biological father William Barnett.
one_line: Character notes for the sitcom That '70s Show, covering Pam Macy, Steven Hyde, and the series finale's Eric-Donna reunion.
key_facts: Pam Macy is played by Jennifer Lyons and is a classmate of the show's main characters.
Pam Macy appeared in the episodes 'Prom Night', 'Romantic Weekend', and 'It's a Wonderful life'.
In 'Prom Night', Michael Kelso took Pam to the prom while temporarily broken up with Jackie.
In 'Romantic Weekend', Kelso was unable to perform sexually and told his friends 'The buffer would n't buff'.
Pam told the whole school about Kelso's failure, which caused everyone to tease Kelso about it.
In the final episode, Eric returns to Point Place for the New Year and he and Donna kiss.
It is presumed that Eric and Donna end up together again at the end of the series and the end of the 1970s.
Steven Hyde is portrayed by Danny Masterson and is Eric's best friend and the anti-establishment member of the group.
By the end of season one, the Formans allow Hyde to move in after he was abandoned by his mother, making him Eric's foster brother.
Hyde dates Jackie for three seasons.
In the final season, Hyde marries an exotic dancer named Samantha.
As Donna points out in 'My Fairy King', Hyde and Samantha are not legally married because Samantha was still married when she married Hyde.
In the seventh season, Hyde meets his biological father William Barnett, played by Tim Reid.
William Barnett is a wealthy black businessman who owns a chain of record stores.
Barnett makes Hyde first the manager, and later the owner, of the Point Place store.
